html:
The Arma were the descendants of the Moroccan soldiers who conquered the Songhai Empire in 1591, and they ruled the middle Niger, around Timbuktu, Gao and Djenné, as the Pashalik of Timbuktu. They are shown here in 1715.

Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur of Morocco sent an army across the Sahara under Judar Pasha, with many Spanish-born soldiers and renegades. Their guns won the Battle of Tondibi. The soldiers stayed, married local women, and their descendants became a hereditary ruling caste. Their name is thought to come from the Arabic word for shooters, al-rumat.

By the mid 17th century Morocco had lost interest, and the Arma pashas were chosen locally, often briefly and violently. Their power shrank. They paid tribute to Tuareg groups and to the Bambara Empire of Ségou, and in the 1820s the Fulani Massina Empire took Timbuktu. The Arma survive as a community in the cities of the Niger bend.
